scenarioStory.history: Patient was skiing at a resort when he caught an edge and twisted his right leg, resulting in immediate severe pain and inability to stand. Ski patrol arrived first and applied an improvised splint with a ski pole before EMS arrival. Patient denies head strike, loss of consciousness, or other injuries.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew arrives to find a 34-year-old male on packed snow with an obvious right lower leg deformity, splinted informally by ski patrol. He is alert, in severe pain, and denies other injuries. → IV obtained, fentanyl given: Crew splints the deformed right lower leg, establishes IV access, and administers weight-based IV fentanyl for severe pain. → Pain reassessed, repeat dose given, transport: Five minutes post-fentanyl, the patient's pain has decreased but is not fully controlled; crew reassesses vital signs and pain score, administers a second weight-based fentanyl dose per protocol, and transports in a position of comfort.

patientInformation.patientCondition: Right lower leg pain after ski fall, unable to bear weight

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew arrives to find a 34-year-old male on packed snow with an obvious right lower leg deformity, splinted informally by ski patrol. He is alert, in severe pain, and denies other injuries.
relatedChecklist: Assess distal pulse, sensation, and movement before splinting
Splint right lower leg in position found; apply ice pack, not directly on skin
Assess pain using Numeric Rating Scale (patient >12 years old)
Fentanyl 84 mcg IV (84 kg × 1 mcg/kg; max initial dose 100 mcg)
Apply capnography to monitor for early hypoventilation after opioid administration

scenarioEvents.name: IV obtained, fentanyl given
scenarioEvents.description: Crew splints the deformed right lower leg, establishes IV access, and administers weight-based IV fentanyl for severe pain.
relatedChecklist: Repeat fentanyl 84 mcg IV 5 min after first dose (84 kg × 1 mcg/kg; pain persists at 4/10)
Transport in position of comfort; reassess vitals and pain score en route

scenarioEvents.name: Pain reassessed, repeat dose given, transport
scenarioEvents.description: Five minutes post-fentanyl, the patient's pain has decreased but is not fully controlled; crew reassesses vital signs and pain score, administers a second weight-based fentanyl dose per protocol, and transports in a position of comfort.

scenarioEvents.name: Fentanyl withheld despite severe pain
scenarioEvents.description: The crew splints the leg but does not administer analgesia despite the patient's continued severe pain, resulting in ongoing tachycardia, hypertension, and patient distress during movement and transport.
relatedChecklist: Recognize undertreated severe pain; administer fentanyl 84 mcg IV (84 kg × 1 mcg/kg; max 100 mcg)
